title: Redwood cost-econ discovery with Kepler Analytics

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11 15:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Rao (Redwood SE); Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Samir Patel (Kepler Head of ML); Maya Reynolds (Kepler CTO); Diego Fuentes (Kepler SRE); Lina Park (Kepler Procurement)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec, um quick note this is Alex, im the AE on your account, Priya is our SE who will geek out on perf details, and Jordan is our CSM who will help run the pilot
[00:10] Maya (Kepler CTO): thanks Alex, excited to chat. we want to understand the unit economics — per token cost and real world tco between hosted and dedicated/private options
[00:22] Priya (Redwood SE): yep, great, we structured this call to map to exactly that — per-token pricing, how batching and KV/prefix caching changes the effective cost, and what Dedicated or Private buys you on predictable throughput and data controls
[00:35] Samir (Kepler Head of ML): quick context — we run a multi-tenant inference stack today on k8s + triton, mostly g4 and some t4 repurposing. latency targets are 120ms p50 for chat assistants, but we also have a batch rerank pipeline that does high qps at night. monthly token volume ~75M tokens across prod, expected to grow 3x next 12 months if we ship new features
[00:58] Diego (Kepler SRE): security is important — we need KMS integration, audit logs, and SOC2 type II. data residency is NA/EU split. we may need VPC peering for dedicated/private
[01:14] Alex: totally — Redwood has Hosted with usage pricing, Dedicated reserved pools with commit discounts, and Private on-prem/VPC options. for economics, most customers start with Hosted, then move to Dedicated when predictable high volume makes the math better
[01:28] Lina (Procurement): budget note — we have an initial monthly budget cap of $15k for inference until we see numbers from a pilot
[01:35] Priya: ok good to know. i'll walk through high-level pricing components — base per-token for Hosted, e.g. for a 8k context model we surface X per 1K tokens, then effective per-token cost drops when you enable batching and reuse via prefix caching or KV cache. Dedicated bundles give lower per-token compute costs but require monthly commit.
[01:55] Samir: can you give an example? numbers are the only thing the execs care about
[02:03] Priya: sure — rough illustrative: Hosted might be $0.0025 per 1K prompt tokens and $0.005 per 1K generated tokens for our mid-sized LLaMA-variant runtimes — that's illustrative, actual depends on model. with batching we can increase GPU utilization so effective cost per generated token drops by ~20-40% depending on latency SLO. prefix caching (for repeated system prompts or shared context) can reduce tokens billed by up to 30% in some chat flows
[02:30] Maya: prefix caching... do you mean we don't resend the whole system prompt each time? how does that affect security/tenant separation
[02:40] Priya: prefix caching stores tokenized KV state on the server side keyed per customer or per conversation, you still control retention and it's encrypted at rest; with Dedicated and Private you get additional isolation options and can bring your own KMS for encryption keys
[03:02] Diego: what about quantization and model variants — can we run a quantized model to save cost while keeping accuracy?
[03:10] Priya: yes — we recommend 4-bit/8-bit quantized variants for high throughput many requests workloads. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles based on your evals; typical tradeoff is slight accuracy drift vs 2-4x lower GPU memory and lower cost per token
[03:29] Samir: ok but how do we decide between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private under our $15k monthly constraint?
[03:36] Alex: good question. high level: Hosted = lowest upfront friction, pay-as-you-go; Dedicated = lower unit cost at the expense of commit; Private = highest control (networking/KMS) and usually higher fixed fees. We can model your 75M tokens — do you have split of prompt vs generated tokens?
[03:55] Samir: average chat turn is 120 input tokens, 80 output tokens historically across assistants. rerank jobs are bigger — 2k tokens input, but scheduled off-peak
[04:06] Priya: okay quick back of envelope: monthly generated tokens ~ (assuming 75M is total tokens) — if 45% are generated that's ~33.75M generated tokens. using the hosted illustrative rates that I mentioned earlier, your monthly hosted cost would be roughly $0.005 * (33.75k units) equals about $168.75 — wait sorry, miscalc, need to spell this out — (Priya laughs) transcription sometimes messy
[04:30] Priya: let me recalc: 33.75M generated tokens is 33,750 units of 1K tokens. at $0.005 per 1K, that's roughly $169. But that's illustrative — real models vary and there are additional infra-ops charges and egress, and model complexity changes price by model family. Also remember batching and caching can drop that effective cost dramatically
[04:55] Maya: that low? I thought costs were higher, are we missing something — we currently pay much more in our in-house setup due to reserve GPU cost and ops overhead
[05:05] Alex: that's right, internal TCO includes hardware depreciation, infra, ops, on-call, and lower GPU utilization. Redwood's hosted rates reflect amortized infra and model licensing. But the real lever: with Dedicated you can get committed capacity discounts — for example a reserved pool can reduce per-token compute cost by 25-45% depending on commit size and model mix.
[05:28] Samir: what about latency implications — we can't accept >200ms tails for chat. batching helps cost but increases latency, right?
[05:35] Priya: partially — we do continuous batching with latency SLOs. batching increases throughput by aggregating small requests, but Redwood's scheduler prioritizes low-latency requests and will route those to fast-paths. In practice you can keep p50/p90 low while still getting batching wins on p95/p99 maybe less. It's a tunable knob per route.
[06:00] Diego: can we pin models and versions? audits want reproducible outputs for given model/version
[06:06] Alex: yes — pinning model version is supported across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Rollouts and canaries are supported; you can freeze model version for production routes
[06:15] Lina: procurement question — for Dedicated, what's the minimum commitment and contract length?
[06:20] Alex: typical starter is a 3-6 month pilot with a nominal monthly commit, then an annual reserved commitment reduces unit costs further. We can propose a pilot that fits your $15k cap — e.g., a 3-month pilot at $12k/month for reserved pool capacity and nightly benchmark runs
[06:36] Samir: what does the pilot include technically?
[06:40] Priya: pilot includes a dedicated GPU pool sized to your target QPS, baseline perf testing (latency and throughput), integration of prefix/KV caching on representative flows, and instrumentation so you can see token-level cost and latency breakdowns in Redwood Console. We also include a short run of our optimize recommendations (batching/quantization suggestions)
[06:58] Maya: will we be able to bring our own keys? we need to use our KMS for encryption-in-use or at least for at-rest keys
[07:05] Alex: yes for Dedicated and Private you can bring your KMS and we expose audit logs and RBAC. For Hosted we offer managed keys but can discuss customer-managed keys for enterprise plans
[07:18] Diego: any network topology examples for VPC peering?
[07:22] Priya: yes we have standard VPC peering, private link, and on-prem connectors for air-gapped. we'll share architecture docs after this call
[07:34] Samir: back to cost — can Priya sketch a more realistic cost ladder using our profile?
[07:40] Priya: sure, i'll propose three scenarios: 1) Hosted baseline with caching off; 2) Hosted with caching and batching optimizations; 3) Dedicated reserved with same optimizations and quantized models. I'll put rough numbers into a spreadsheet and show break-even points vs commit size
[07:55] Priya: for example, with your 75M tokens/month, scenario 1 might be $X, scenario 2 reduces by 25% due to caching/batching, scenario 3 reduces another 20-30% if you commit to Dedicated and switch to quantized runtimes for specific routes
[08:12] Maya: important metric for us is cost per answered query where we count full conversation tokens. can you map to that?
[08:18] Alex: yes, we'll map to cost per session/average user per month too in the spreadsheet
[08:24] Lina: procurement needs a sample SOW and cancellation terms for pilot
[08:29] Jordan (CSM): we'll include an SOW template in the follow-up pack and outline termination terms for the pilot period
[08:36] Samir: are there any hidden costs — like egress, logging, or additional instrumentation fees?
[08:41] Priya: good point — egress charges are separate if you route large vector embeddings or heavy downloads. Logging/observability has tiered retention; the console has token-level cost breakdown but long-term storage of traces is an add-on. We'll call these out in the cost model spreadsheet
[09:00] Diego: for our reranking pipelines that run nightly and are batch heavy, can Redwood schedule spot-like capacity or cheaper compute windows?
[09:07] Priya: yes — we support burst capacity and scheduled batch windows on Dedicated; cost is lower for off-peak usage. For Hosted we can route heavy batch jobs to cheaper backends where available
[09:20] Samir: any customer examples with similar profile?
[09:23] Alex: we have a fintech customer with mixed chat+batch that moved to Dedicated and saw 30% lower unit cost and much less ops overhead. we'll anonymize and share the case study
[09:33] Maya: ok would like to see the cost model and case study; if the numbers look good execs will sign pilot next week
[09:41] Alex: sounds good. action items: we'll send cost-model, SOW, and benchmark plan. also we should schedule a 60-90 minute technical deep-dive with your SREs to go over VPC and KMS details
[09:55] Priya: quick technical note — to get maximum caching benefit you need stable conversation ids and not re-embedding the entire context each turn. small SDK changes on client side can yield big token savings
[10:08] Samir: that sounds doable, we'll have engs look at SDK changes as part of pilot
[10:15] Diego: what's the expected timeline to get a dedicated pool standing up for the pilot?
[10:19] Priya: we can provision a pilot pool within a week of contract signature for common regions; on-prem private deployments take longer (4-8 weeks)
[10:27] Lina: procurement will need a PoC SOW and an invoice template
[10:31] Jordan: we'll attach those to the follow-up email
[10:35] Alex: any other questions on economics?
[10:38] Maya: one more — how do you surface cost per route in the console? can we set alerts on daily spend?
[10:44] Priya: yes route-level dashboards, token-per-route cost breakdowns, and alerting for spend thresholds and anomalous usage are supported
[10:52] Samir: great. summary for me — send cost model with Hosted/Dedicated/Private scenarios, propose pilot SOW within $15k monthly cap, plan benchmark with sample prompts, and schedule deep dive on security
[10:58] Alex: exactly. we'll get that out tomorrow; Priya will own benchmark plan, I'll own pricing and SOW, Jordan will own procurement docs
[11:05] Maya: thanks all, look forward to the follow-up
[11:09] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack and schedule next meeting

End of transcript

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript has occasional mis-transcriptions and numbers might be off in quick in-call calc — follow-up spreadsheet will have definitive numbers.
